props.title: Wobble Palace

sections.content: **Wobble Palace (2018)** (2018) represents a sharp examination of millennial relationships in the digital age, following a couple who decides to spend their last weekend together by splitting their shared apartment - one gets it Saturday, the other Sunday. Director Eugene Kotlyarenko crafts a hyper-modern comedy that feels like **Scenes from a Marriage** (1973) filtered through Instagram stories. The film's experimental approach mirrors similarly boundary-pushing relationship studies like **500 Days of Summer** (2009) and **Blue Valentine** (2010), but with a distinctly extremely-online aesthetic.

sections.content: What makes **Wobble Palace** particularly fascinating is how it captures the specific anxieties of relationships in the late 2010s. Like **Her** (2013) and **Black Mirror's** San Junipero episode (2016), it explores how technology mediates our most intimate connections. The film's split narrative structure, giving each partner their own day to spiral through dating apps and questionable decisions, cleverly mirrors the fractured nature of modern attention spans and relationships.

The film's visual style embraces the aesthetic of social media, similar to how **Tangerine** (2015) used iPhone cinematography to capture a raw slice of LA life. Kotlyarenko employs text messages, dating app interfaces, and social media posts as both storytelling devices and commentary on how we construct our digital identities. This approach feels spiritually connected to films like **Creative Control** (2015) and **Nerve** (2016), which also explore technology's impact on relationships and identity. sections.content: The film's exploration of performative relationships shares DNA with **The King of Staten Island** (2020) and **Palm Springs** (2020) in how it examines millennials grappling with commitment and authenticity. The characters' constant documentation of their lives - even during their breakup - speaks to themes similar to those in **Cam** (2018) and **Profile** (2018), where digital identity becomes inseparable from reality.
